identity.name: County and Duchy of Luxembourg (House of Luxembourg)

land.text: the duchy of Luxembourg, which 'Sigismund of Luxembourg lost ... to his niece Elisabeth' in 1411

successors.note: The same land and title under Elisabeth of Gorlitz (1411-1443); the duchy-of-luxembourg dossier starts in 1411 on the same two pages, so the two are one state under two houses and should share a colour. Cliopatria keeps this row to 1414 and starts the other in 1429.

correction.text: unchanged, for 1260-1263 only: Henry V's Luxembourg, Laroche and Arlon with the Namur lands he held as 'Marquis of Namur 1256-1264'

keyframe_review.note: 7.6 k km2 for 1260-1271. The Namur part (12 cells, about 3 k km2, bbox 4.56-5.33 E) is the western limb; Henry seized Namur in 1256 and the infobox ends his marquisate in 1264 when Guy retook it, so the outline holds to 1263. The page names Namur but no boundary; the cells' position is my reading. 1264-1271 are the new keyframe below.

correction.text: Luxembourg, Laroche and Arlon without Namur, from the infobox end of Henry V's Marquis of Namur (1264)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1264-1271: Cliopatria keeps the Namur limb to 1271 and drops it in 1272; the page ends the marquisate in 1264.

5.8 k km2 for 1272-1293 (from 1264 with the keyframe above): Luxembourg, Laroche and Arlon, 'Count of Luxembourg 1247-1281' (infobox), Henry VI after 1281 (the page gives no date for the succession). Neither page dates a boundary here.

5.7 k km2 (one cell less than 1272). The Duchy page says 'The ducal lands had been formed in 1353 by integration of the old County of Luxembourg' with Arlon, Durbuy, La Roche and the districts of Thionville, Bitburg and Marville; Cliopatria draws that enlargement only in 1363, so this outline holds to 1352 and the new keyframe below covers 1353-1362.

correction.text: the 1363 outline carried back to 1353, the year the ducal lands were formed

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1353-1362: 'The ducal lands had been formed in 1353 by integration of the old County of Luxembourg'; 'in 1354, Emperor Charles IV elevated it to the status of a duchy for his brother Wenceslaus'. The 17 added cells lie inside Cliopatria's Holy Roman Empire Minor States in 1350-1362.

10.2 k km2 for 1363-1394 (from 1353 with the keyframe above). The Duchy page, the Wenceslaus I page and the dynasty page give no area; Cliopatria's Duchy of Luxembourg row (10.3 k km2, 1429) is the same land.

The identical 10.2 k km2 outline for 1395-1406. Wenceslaus was 'declared deposed by the prince-electors in 1400'; the pages date no change of the duchy's lands, and the pledges of the duchy (to Jobst of Moravia in 1388, to Louis of Orleans in 1402) are on none of the five pages opened.

correction.text: unchanged, for 1407-1411 only; 1412-1414 is Elisabeth of Gorlitz's duchy, carried by the duchy-of-luxembourg dossier

keyframe_review.note: 10.2 k km2. 'Elisabeth ... reigned as Duchess of Luxembourg from 1411 to 1443' (Elizabeth of Gorlitz page); the Duchy page: 'In 1411, Sigismund of Luxembourg lost the duchy to his niece Elisabeth because he defaulted on a loan.' Both pages' infoboxes give 1415 for her reign, which the text contradicts.

region.text: Luxembourg, Laroche and Arlon, with Namur

ledger.note: 1260: Count Henry V holds Luxembourg, Laroche, Arlon and Namur. 'Henry inherited Luxembourg and Laroche following the death of his mother, Ermesinde, in 1247'; 'In 1256, Henry seized Namur'; Arlon came to him in 1226. The county is older than Cliopatria's row, which starts here.

region.text: the Namur lands on the west side of the 1260 outline (bbox 4.56-5.33 E, 49.9-50.5 N, about 3 k km2) that Henry V held as Marquis of Namur 1256-1264

ledger.note: 1264: Henry V loses Namur to Guy of Flanders. Infobox 'Marquis of Namur 1256-1264'; 'Baldwin sold his rights to Namur to Guy, Count of Flanders, who retook the margraviate from Henry.' The page does not date the retaking or the peace (Guy married Henry's daughter Isabelle); 1264 is the infobox year.

region.text: the county of Durbuy and the districts of Thionville, Bitburg and Marville, the south, west and east additions of the 1363 outline (about 4.3 k km2)

ledger.note: 1353: the ducal lands are formed. 'The ducal lands had been formed in 1353 by integration of the old County of Luxembourg'; they then took in the Marquisate of Arlon, Durbuy, La Roche and 'the districts of Thionville, Bitburg, and Marville'. The page does not say who held those districts before; they sit inside Cliopatria's Minor States lump until 1362.

1354: Charles IV raises Luxembourg to a duchy for his half-brother Wenceslaus. Infobox: Duke of Luxembourg '13 March 1354 - 7 December 1383'; 'In 1354 Charles raised Luxembourg to the status of a duchy.' The Duchy page also dates the elevation to 1354 and the grant of the county to Wenceslaus to 1353.

1411: Sigismund loses Luxembourg to his niece Elisabeth of Gorlitz. 'In 1411, Sigismund of Luxembourg lost the duchy to his niece Elisabeth because he defaulted on a loan.' The Elizabeth page: 'reigned as Duchess of Luxembourg from 1411 to 1443'. The duchy goes on as duchy-of-luxembourg.

wars.name: Henry V's seizure and loss of Namur (1256-1264)

zones.text: the Namur lands on the west side of the 1260 outline (bbox 4.56-5.33 E, 49.9-50.5 N, about 3 k km2) that Henry V held as Marquis of Namur 1256-1264

wars.outcome: Henry V seized Namur in 1256 while Baldwin II was away as emperor in Constantinople; Baldwin sold his rights to Guy, Count of Flanders, who retook the margraviate (infobox: Henry marquis 1256-1264); peace followed and Guy married Henry's daughter Isabelle.
wars.note: The page gives no campaign, battle or date for Guy's retaking, so no contest is entered between 1260 and 1264.

wars.name: Luxembourg-Bar war (Prény 1266)
wars.outcome: 'Henry was captured in battle at Prény on 14 September 1266'; on 8 September 1268 Louis IX arbitrated and Henry was freed, keeping Ligny under Barrois suzerainty.
wars.note: Ligny came to Henry through his 1240 marriage to Margaret of Bar and lies outside the drawn outline. The page also says Henry backed Duke Frederick III of Lorraine against the bishops of Metz while Theobald II of Bar sided with the bishop, undated.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary; the outlines are Cliopatria's approximations of a county of scattered fiefs (Luxembourg, Laroche, Arlon, Durbuy, Thionville, Bitburg, Marville).

notes:
WHAT THIS ROW IS. Cliopatria's 'House of Luxembourg' (1260-1414, 6 shapes, 5.7-10.2 k km2) is the County of Luxembourg (a duchy from 1354) under Henry V and his successors, not the dynasty's Bohemian, German or Brandenburg lands. Name kept as the display of the land; Wikipedia article and Wikidata are the dynasty's, as Cliopatria gives them.

BOUNDARY WITH duchy-of-luxembourg. That dossier (another batch) starts in 1411 and its notes ask this dossier to end its Luxembourg lands at 1410. Both pages opened give 1411 for Elisabeth, so this dossier ends in 1411 and the 1411 year overlaps; the later dossier should win in 1411. Cliopatria's 1407 shape runs to 1414, so 1412-1414 are left to the duchy dossier. The two are one state (same land, title and capital) under two houses; the colour agent should give them one colour.

CORRECTIONS. (1) Namur: the 1260 outline's western limb is Henry V's Namur (infobox 1256-1264); (2) the 1363 enlargement belongs to 1353 (Duchy page), 10 years earlier. The cells' identification with Namur and with the Thionville, Bitburg and Marville districts rests on their position (bbox) and not on a boundary given by any page.

NOT SETTLED. (a) No infobox area on any page opened, so Cliopatria's areas could not be compared. (b) The pledges of the duchy to Jobst of Moravia (1388) and Louis of Orleans (1402/1407) and the reigns of Wenceslaus II/IV and Sigismund as dukes are on none of the five pages (the dynasty page has one Wenceslaus, 1361-1419); nothing is entered for 1384-1410. Sigismund is not in the Duchy infobox's list. (c) The Duchy page puts the Burgundian takeover in 1443 (infobox, text) and 1444 (text, payment); that is the other dossier's. (d) 1288 Worringen: 'All of his sons perished in the Battle of Worringen in 1288' (Henry V page) and Henry VI fell there; no page opened names the war's sides or any land, so no war is entered. (e) Wenceslaus I held Brabant and Limburg with Joanna from 1355 (infobox 1355-1383) and Charles IV acquired Brandenburg in 1373 (dynasty page): personal unions outside this row, belonging to the county-of-brabant and margraviate-of-brandenburg dossiers. (f) No ruler strip: the pages give no continuous list with years. (g) The county is older than 1260 (Duchy page timeline 'Duchy of Luxembourg (1059-1443)'; Henry V count from 1247); predecessors left empty because the row starts here.

Counterparts without a dossier: county-of-namur (Duchy page timeline 'County of Namur (981-1421)'). The County of Bar is the existing duchy-of-bar dossier (slug corrected by reviewer eu-09-e). Gazetteer: no new names used.
